text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches when they build something new, like a login page or a bug fix. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project safe and organised. If something goes wrong, the main branch stays clean. Learning branches helps you work better with a team and manage your code more easily.
